title: Owen Muir-Centric Updates!
subtitle: A few self-interest updates for my readers....
body_html:
The Frontier Psychiatrist is written— mostly— by Owen Scott Muir, M.D., DFAACAP. I have gigs other than writing this. However, writing this just got a little more official! I'm thrilled to welcome the clinical team at Heading Health, a leading intervention practice featuring TMS, ketamine, and Spravato in Texas, as paid subscribers to the newsletter! This is my second corporate group after my friends at GrayMatters Health joined last year. I'm thrilled to have an entire group of subscribers because it validates my gigantic ego. Sorry, my hypothesis is that funny and engaging content about health is worth something to somebody.

Seriously though, I'm humbled that my readers keep reading, so I keep writing. This newsletter and podcast exist to advance my agenda of the world with less suffering and a little bit more fun in learning about it.

I have a few updates about me and the work that I do! I'm thrilled to announce that I'll be attending the thinc360 conference in Washington, DC, next week, as my team at Acacia Clinics is in the running for the best mental health value award!

Do I have more than one team? Yes. I'm prolific. As a summary of this—for those who don't stalk me on LinkedIn—here is my current array of gigs:

Co-Founder: Fermata

(A New York City-based clinic and contract research organization)

Co-founder: Breakthrough6

(A scalable Neuromodulation-First platform solution for hospitals and communities).

Co-Founder: RAMHT

(Rapid-acting mental health treatment is a recurring conference series— co-created with Grady Hannah…think of it as the live-action version of this newsletter)

Chief Medical Officer, iRxReminder

(A medical device company focusing on medication adherence and AI diagnostics)

Senior Vice President, Strategy, Acacia Clinics

(The leading interventional Neuromodulation clinic in the world!)

Additionally, I am a consultant to…

Videra Health — a leader in video-based AI assessment tools that just announced a $5.6 million funding round!

Magnus Medical is a commercial-stage medical device company that is bringing SAINT neuromodulation to the market.

Outro Health — a health technology and services company helping individuals taper off medication!

And some other gigs that are under NDA…

I still see patients at Fermata and Acacia, and I'm proud to continue teaching and learning at conferences and teaching hospitals. I am also probably forgetting something!

How do I do it all? I don't watch a lot of TV. I write every day, so it gets faster. And, honestly, I don't have a choice. I want to see a better world, and I'm not independently wealthy—I can’t just pay for that future to come about. Thus, there's work to do! I see a future that has less suffering, more effective treatments, more rapidly deployed, faster acting, safer, with less inpatient psychiatric hospitalization and dramatically less restraint and seclusion. I want to see people get well. I don't want to sit and wait for it to happen. It needs to be less harmful and more effective.

I'm trying to do the work to make the change in the world that I want to see—less death and desperation, and more hope. I think technology can get us there when compassion and sense are augmented.

I think part of the answer is employer groups need to get serious about compliance with the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2021, which makes it the fiduciary duty of employers to comply with ERISA. I deeply mourn the passing of Marshall Allen, a remarkable reporter and driver of change in our world; he passed away abruptly this past week. But with out him, that law would not have been passed.

I'll point out that there are already several lawsuits against employer groups by their employees, to whom they have a fiduciary duty, in keeping with arguments I've made long before those lawsuits were filed. Imagine if the Oracle of Delphi only gave you bad news about pending litigation. That’s me! I imagine we're going to have lawsuits for mental health parity violations. That's part of the law, too, thanks to the Accountable Care Act. I don't see any way towards parity of better treatments. There just aren't enough treaters to keep up with the demand for (albeit ineffective) treatment. We need to change the underlying assumptions of what's possible. This means treatments need to be better, not just for the individual suffering, but for the employers paying for it, because otherwise, there's a real problem for everybody.

We need a better world, but it must also be safer, cheaper, more effective, and leave all of us in better shape.

Join me.

Subscribe now
